A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MERGE3 and contain readable main text and Appendices A–D. Full text comparison and rendered-page inspection establish that the scientific content is identical; differences concern version marking and bibliography presentation.

before.justification: v2 reports original estimator evaluations, cross-lingual and multilingual merging experiments, self-merging controls, and throughput measurements in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix C, including estimator evaluations, multilingual merging, self-merging controls, and throughput measurements.

M1.justification: The Extract–Estimate–Evolve procedure, MP-IRT and GMP-IRT estimators, merging strategies, evolutionary search, and Algorithm 1 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five estimator benchmarks: GSM8K, Winogrande, TruthfulQA, HellaSwag, and ARC. Cross-lingual, multilingual, and appendix language scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including P-IRT, GP-IRT, random sampling, Task Arithmetic, TIES-DARE, SLERP, EvoLLM-JP-7B, and endpoint models. Appendix C retains the same extraction-method comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B.3 retain identical splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, and fitness-subset sizes. Evolutionary experiments still specify population size 25 and seven iterations.

E4.justification: Appendix C preserves the same sampling-strategy comparisons, sample-size sensitivity analyses, ability-estimation analyses, and Italian self-merging control. No ablation or robustness analysis is added, removed, or revised.

E5.justification: The plotted error bars and uncertainty bands, variability discussion, and self-merging hypothesis framing are unchanged. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are identical throughout. For example, Table 1 retains MERGE3 accuracies of 0.69, 0.79, 0.72, and 0.69 for Italian, English, German, and Dutch; Figure 6 and Table 7 retain the same Japanese GSM8K results.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, the estimator equations, Section 5's definitions and theoretical guarantees, Appendix C.1's clustering derivations, and Appendix D's proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about computational savings, consumer-GPU feasibility, cross-lingual transfer, multilingual performance, theoretical guarantees, and the software contribution.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of linear ability inheritance, weight interference, cross-lingual synergy, self-merging evidence, and random sampling's practicality. Applicability qualifications and limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: The library description, model identifiers, IRT settings, translation and evaluation procedures, NVIDIA 4090 hardware details, and code and supplementary-material access statements remain identical.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Gargiulo et al.'s Task Singular Vectors entry receives only a preprint-to-CVPR publication-metadata update; its citation and role in the related-work discussion remain the same.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are confined to the arXiv version/date stamp and the Task Singular Vectors bibliography entry, which replaces its arXiv URL with 'In Proc. CVPR, 2025.' Main-text and appendix prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened reference reflows bibliography pages 10–11, including moving Shoemake (1985) from page 11 to page 10. All figures, tables, algorithms, and scientific page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, supporting evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and proofs are identical, including the appendices. Updating one reference's publication details and adjusting bibliography flow and version marking do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
